issues: fin/cmd_bills.py bill_pay never checks the type of --account (invoice_pay in fin/cmd_invoicing.py requires an asset account), and neither command checks the currency of --account or of an existing Assets:Receivable / Liabilities:Payable, so a currency mismatch fails with a misleading 'transaction does not balance' error from Ctx.post.

Logic is duplicated across modules: parse_posting appears in both fin/cmd_books.py and fin/cmd_import.py; the tax-rate lookup appears in cmd_invoicing.tax_rate and cmd_bills.parse_line; the subtree test is written three ways (cmd_books.under, an inline startswith in cmd_import.report_budget, and a substr() SQL clause in cmd_reports.ledger); and the role rules exist in both cli.check_permission and api.authorize.

fin/cmd_reports.py trial_balance and balance_sheet convert and round each account separately before summing, so with several currencies total_debit can differ from total_credit, and total_assets from total_liabilities + total_equity, by a few cents, even though the spec requires them to be equal.

fin/api.py turns each request into CLI argv strings and re-parses them with argparse, so input is validated indirectly: a posting account containing '=' is split in the wrong place, a negative payment amount becomes an argparse 'unrecognized option' error, and any sqlite3.OperationalError (for example 'database is locked' under ThreadingHTTPServer) returns a generic 500.

fin/cmd_import.py recurring_add validates by posting a trial transaction dated on the start date, so adding a recurring entry whose start falls in a closed period fails even though recurring add creates no transaction, and validation depends on side effects inside a savepoint.

The tests seed data by writing straight to SQL (tests/test_taxrecon.py make_doc/make_txn, tests/test_bills.py setUp), which ties them to the schema; the tax report is tested only on hand-made rows, not on real invoices and bills; and tests/test_core_admin.py checks users, audit and periods in a single combined test.
strengths: fin/core.py gives one Ctx with a single validated post() path, the fmt/q money helpers and the fx rate lookup, and cli.run wraps every command in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, so failures are atomic and init removes the half-created database file.
Money is handled as Decimal from parsing to storage (stored as TEXT strings), and every SQL statement uses parameters; the only f-string SQL interpolates fixed table names and column constants.

The command modules are small and follow one shared register/set_defaults(func, perm) pattern, and functions are short with clear names (for example category_for, occurrence, bucket, _balance_sheet_at).
